name: Hellas Planitia
mission: None (orbiters only - studied by Mars Global Surveyor MOLA and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter)
terrain: Floor of a 2300 km impact basin, 7152 m below the Martian datum - the lowest point on Mars
temperature_notes: Southern mid-latitude (42 deg S); deep basin traps the thickest air on Mars, but winters are still far below freezing
water_ice: Pressure at the floor is about 12.4 mbar, above the triple point of water, so liquid water is theoretically possible there; gullies in Dao Vallis and Reull Vallis may have carried water; the basin may once have held lakes and glaciers
hazards: A known source of global dust storms; the basin rim rises up to 9000 m above the floor
description: The deepest hole on Mars - air pressure there is double the Martian average, and it is one of the least irradiated places on the planet. But it spawns planet-wide dust storms.

name: Arcadia Planitia
mission: None (orbiters only - Mars Odyssey THEMIS, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter)
terrain: Smooth northern lowland plain; grooves and ridges formed by near-surface ice processes
temperature_notes: High latitude (about 47 deg N), like Utopia - long cold winters, much less warmth than equatorial sites
water_ice: NASA's ice map shows water ice less than 30 cm (about 1 foot) below the surface across large areas - NASA calls it the most tempting northern-hemisphere target for astronauts
hazards: Areas of fine dust where a lander could sink (the black zones on NASA's ice map); cold winters
description: The shallowest water ice on Mars - in places you could dig it up with a shovel. The top pick for a future astronaut base in the northern hemisphere.

name: Mawrth Vallis
mission: None landed - was a finalist landing site for both Curiosity (MSL) and ESA's ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover
terrain: Ancient outflow channel cutting between highlands and lowlands, lined with layered clay-rich deposits
temperature_notes: Northern mid-latitude (about 23 deg N) - warmer than the high latitudes, still well below freezing
water_ice: One of the largest exposures of water-formed clay minerals on Mars; clays and a possible delta mean water sat here for a very long time - but no confirmed accessible ice
hazards: Channel and layered terrain is rougher than a plain; dust
description: A 636 km channel that once poured floods onto the northern plains, lined with water-made clays. A geologist's dream - great science, rougher ground to live on.

name: Meridiani Planum
mission: Opportunity rover (NASA, landed 25 Jan 2004, operated 14+ years) - also the target of ESA's Schiaparelli lander (2016)
terrain: Famously flat plain, chosen for landing safety - few rocks and craters; 22 km Endeavour crater lies to the west
temperature_notes: On the equator (0.2 deg N) - the warmest and sunniest region on Mars, though still freezing most of the time
water_ice: Gray hematite and sulfate minerals (jarosite) show the ground was soaked in salty, acidic water long ago; the water is locked in minerals, not an ice deposit
hazards: Dust - the 2018 global dust storm ended Opportunity's 14-year mission by covering its solar panels
description: Where Opportunity drove for 14 years - the flattest, sunniest proven real estate on Mars, with evidence of long-ago water. Great solar power, but no ice to drink.

name: Planum Boreum
mission: None landed at the pole (orbiters only: MRO, Mars Express; Phoenix landed nearby at 68 deg N in 2008)
terrain: North polar ice cap about 1000 km across; layered water-ice deposits with spiral troughs, ringed by dune fields
temperature_notes: The pole (90 deg N) - below -125 C in winter, with months of polar night; the coldest place on Mars
water_ice: Permanent water-ice cap about 2 km thick, holding around 1.2 million cubic km of water - nearly unlimited ice, though part is covered by seasonal CO2 frost
hazards: Extreme cold; CO2 snowfall in winter; polar storms with winds up to 400 km/h; months of darkness
description: Mars' north pole: an ocean of frozen water nearly half the size of Greenland's ice sheet. Water is everywhere - but the cold, darkness and storms make it the hardest place to live.
